title: Ops Lifeline: Quickpatch Registry & Observability Instrumentation
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: On-call engineers and SREs repeatedly re-author similar remediation steps during incidents (DB failover, cache flush, model fallback). We need a lightweight, discoverable Quickpatch Registry: a curated catalog of parameterized remediation recipes (typed inputs, pre-checks, rollback steps) that can be executed as runbook-tasks from the support console or CLI.

Goal: Ship a first-class Quickpatch Registry service and an observability instrumentation connector so every quickpatch execution emits structured telemetry, audit trails, and post-run quality signals. The registry must support versioning, canary rollout of patch changes, dry-run, and safe RBAC gates. Integrations: Support Console UI (search & preview), opsctl CLI execute/dry-run, and runbooks-as-tasks conversion pipeline that maps existing runbooks to quickpatch artifacts.

Constraints and non-goals: This project does not include full on-prem deployment automation for Private customers (that will be follow-up). We will not implement custom KMS flows in v1 — use existing KMS integration for secrets used by quickpatch steps. Prioritize safety (pre-checks, idempotency hooks) and telemetry to enable postmortems and regression detection.
acceptance_criteria: Service + lightweight metadata store deployed: quickpatches have name, description, inputs schema, pre-checks, steps, rollback, owner, and semantic version
Support Console: search, preview, and execute/dry-run flows with input validation and explicit RBAC enforcement
opsctl CLI: list, describe, dry-run, and execute commands that map to the same API surface as the console
Instrumentation: every execution emits structured events (start, pre-check result, step-level events, success/failure, rollback) to our telemetry pipeline with patch_id and run_id
Safety: pre-checks run automatically and block execution on failure; executions require explicit confirmation when high-impact tag is present
Telemetry + Dashboard: a basic Quickpatch execution dashboard (counts, success rate, mean time-to-execute, top failing patches) is available in console-2026.03 release
comments: 2026-01-20 — Spike complete: prototype metadata model (name, inputs-schema JSON Schema, pre-checks, steps list, rollback) and minimal API. Verified we can store artifacts in S3 with metadata index in Dynamo (latency acceptable).
2026-01-28 — Design review: PM and SRE asked for explicit failure modes and a required 'safety-level' tag (low/medium/high) that toggles confirmation and dry-run by default for high-impact patches.

2026-02-10 — Implementation: API scaffold merged (PR #5823). Started on console search UI and opsctl CLI bindings. Chose to reuse existing auth middleware and audit-log pipeline to avoid new product infra surface in v1.

2026-02-24 — Review feedback: Security requested a list of allowed external commands and a capability whitelist for cloud-only quickpatches; engineering proposes an allowlist and a runtime sandbox check. Added as TODO for v1 gating.

2026-03-03 — Telemetry spike: implemented event schema and validated with synthetic executions — step timing, pre-check statuses, and run metadata are present. Hooked into trace correlation (trace_id -> run_id).

2026-03-09 — Blocker: RBAC policy mapping for nested org teams needs clarification from Identity team. Raised dependency ENG-314162 for policy mapping work; paused final production rollout until mapping is resolved.

2026-03-10 — Plan: unblock path by shipping an opt-in org-scoped RBAC mode and default to team-owned quickpatches for public rollout. Finish console flows and schedule QA runbook-dryrun tests next week.
next_steps: Complete console execution UI (input validation + confirmation flows)
Finish opsctl integration and e2e dry-run tests against staging
Wire up telemetry dashboard panels and create alert for regression in quickpatch success rate
Coordinate a quick training session for SREs and oncall squad; prepare rollout notes
